item.title: Gandhi's letter to India, as told through TOI
item.description: From his South Africa years to the freedom struggle, Mahatma Gandhi repeatedly used newspapers to address India’s public. Alok Sharma sifts through letters Gandhi wrote to TOI, illuminating his positions on Satyagraha, the Rowlatt Act, Dalit representation, Hindu-Muslim unity and the hardships faced by Indians in South Africa.

item.title: MacKenzie Scott helped abolish $40B in medical debt; how mechanics work
item.description: MacKenzie Scott is leading the charge in medical debt relief, having made groundbreaking donations that freed over $40 billion for families burdened by this often overwhelming responsibility. Her innovative approach, which involves acquiring debt at minimal costs for cancellation, has inspired other billionaires to make similar contributions. Yet, the call for broader policy reform lingers, revealing the constraints of this philanthropic model.

item.description: A Bengaluru couple was discovered deceased in their rented home early Thursday morning. The husband, Sumant Jain, reportedly sent a chilling voice message to his mother. He mentioned an argument with his wife, Padmavathi, before his death. Padmavathi's family has accused her husband of murder and subsequent suicide. Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding their deaths.

item.title: Oracle prepares fresh layoffs before September 1, asks managers to name who goes
item.description: Oracle is planning fresh layoffs this month, with managers reportedly asked to identify employees whose roles will go before its second fiscal quarter opens on September 1. Some teams face double-digit percentage cuts. The move follows a year in which Oracle eliminated 21,000 jobs, spent $1.8 billion on restructuring, and poured $55.7 billion into AI data centres.

item.title: Cockroaches, expired food: FDA suspends licences of Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart hubs
item.description: The Maharashtra FDA took decisive action by suspending licenses for fourteen food outlets affiliated with quick-commerce services like Blinkit and Zepto, citing significant hygiene breaches. Inspections uncovered problems in pest management, storage conditions, and temperature regulation. In response, some establishments were temporarily closed, while others received official notices to rectify non-compliance, highlighting the urgent need for online food operators to maintain strict safety standards.

item.title: 'I shot him': Luigi Mangione pleads guilty to killing United Healthcare CEO
item.description: Luigi Mangione has confessed to the fatal shooting of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson in Manhattan. He has entered a guilty plea for federal stalking charges in connection to the incident. This plea addresses one of two criminal cases targeting Mangione, while he is still preparing for a state murder trial set for September. During the investigation, authorities found a 3D-printed gun along with a notebook.

item.title: Marcus Aurelius' quote on how perception shapes what we hear and see
item.description: Marcus Aurelius, the philosopher-king of Rome, turned to Stoicism as a means to master the trials of existence. He championed the ability to control one's own reactions, urging acceptance of circumstances beyond personal control. His focus on virtue over fleeting fame, wealth, or power is vividly captured in his reflections, Meditations, which continue to provide valuable insights for overcoming life's challenges and uncertainties.

item.title: LS panel sends notice to Rahul over 'unparliamentary' remarks against Shah
item.description: Rahul Gandhi has been served a Lok Sabha notice regarding privilege complaints raised by BJP MPs Anurag Thakur and Sanjay Jaiswal. The complaints accuse Gandhi of using inappropriate and disrespectful language towards Amit Shah. He is required to submit a response to the Secretariat by August 28, after which the Speaker will assess both the complaints and his reply.

item.title: Brunei Sultan strips daughter-in-law of royal title over 'unbecoming conduct'
item.description: Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah of Brunei has stripped daughter-in-law Pengiran Raabi’atul Adawiyyah of her royal title over conduct deemed “unbecoming” of a royal spouse. The palace said her actions tarnished the monarchy’s reputation and showed disrespect towards the Sultan. Raabi’atul remains married to Prince Abdul Malik, with no divorce announced, while their four daughters retain their titles.

item.title: Male redback spiders somersault directly towards a female’s fangs during mating
item.description: Recent research uncovers that a singular genetic region governs the intricate somersaulting behavior of male redback spiders during mating rituals. This fascinating behavior, crucial for reproduction, is inherited through the X chromosome. Experimental hybrids indicate that this somersault characteristic is not only recessive but also X-linked. Conversely, abdominal narrowing seems influenced by a combination of multiple genes and environmental conditions, challenging traditional views on the complexity of genetic traits.

item.title: Former slave and Union soldier lost Nebraska homestead, later owned 2,000 acres
item.description: Escaping the bonds of slavery, Robert Ball Anderson became a proud soldier in the Union Army. Despite facing significant obstacles in farming caused by severe weather and pests, he dedicated himself to saving money through various jobs, including cooking for railroads. His efforts culminated in owning more than two thousand acres of fertile land, exemplifying the strength and resilience of African Americans in achieving landownership across the Great Plains.
